criteria.name: FR and NFR Traceability to Discovery Q&A
criteria.description: Every FR- and NFR- cites at least one valid Q- from qa_log.json. Every requirement directly traces to client statements.

scale.3: 100% of FRs and NFRs cite valid [Q-###] sources that explicitly support the requirement.
scale.2: All FRs and NFRs cite sources, but 1 citation points to general context rather than specific Q-.
scale.1: One or more FRs or NFRs lack citations [Q-###].
scale.0: No requirements cite sources or citations are fabricated.

criteria.name: Strict ISO/IEC 29148 FR vs NFR Classification
criteria.description: Strict separation: FRs contain only user workflows/capabilities. Latency, performance, local storage, security, and offline constraints are filed as NFRs. No user features filed as NFRs.

scale.3: Flawless classification: zero technical, latency, storage, or offline constraints misfiled in FR; zero functional capabilities misfiled in NFR.
scale.2: Minor boundary ambiguity in 1 item, but no clear misclassification.
scale.1: 1 performance/storage constraint misfiled as FR, or 1 functional capability misfiled as NFR.
scale.0: Widespread misclassification between functional and non-functional requirements.

criteria.name: Unambiguous and Testable Requirements
criteria.description: No vague qualitative words left ('fast', 'secure', 'many users', 'intuitive'). Every quality has a concrete number, measurable benchmark, or explicit yes/no test per ISO 29148.

scale.3: All requirements are verifiable, atomic, and quantified with concrete numbers or objective yes/no tests.
scale.2: Nearly all requirements quantified; 1 requirement has slightly broad wording.
scale.1: Contains vague terms ('fast', 'seamless', 'scalable') without numbers or objective tests.

criteria.name: Persona Grounding and 5 Whys Needs
criteria.description: Every FR- traces to a stated persona (P-#) and documents the need behind it (5 Whys). Zero invented roles or boilerplate personas.

scale.3: Personas are 100% grounded in client discovery with context and tech comfort. Every FR- lists persona and root need.
scale.2: Personas grounded, but 1-2 FRs have brief need descriptions.
scale.1: Missing persona linkage on some FRs or contains unstated/invented roles.
scale.0: Personas invented or entirely missing from requirements.

criteria.name: End-to-End User Journeys (J-)
criteria.description: Main user journeys (J-#) documented step-by-step from start to finish with clear outcomes and citations.

scale.3: Complete end-to-end user journeys with step -> step -> outcome flow and valid Q- citations.
scale.2: Journeys present with start-to-finish flow, but 1 journey lacks explicit outcome step.

criteria.name: Conflict, Assumption, and Open Question Handling
criteria.description: Conflicts between answers raised as OQ- citing conflicting Q-s. Unstated or estimated items recorded as ASM- with reason and risk. No silent resolution.

scale.3: Rigorous conflict/gap handling: conflicts raised with dual citations; assumptions explicitly stated with reason and risk; zero silent assumptions.
scale.2: Assumptions recorded, but minor omission in risk explanation.
scale.1: Unstated items presented as client facts without ASM- or OQ- designation.
scale.0: Silent resolution of conflicts or rampant unflagged assumptions.

criteria.name: Scope, Timeline, and Budget Feasibility
criteria.description: Scope fits stated timeline and budget with MoSCoW prioritization. Items outside v1 boundary explicitly categorized in Won't (v1) with client rationale.

scale.3: Realistic MoSCoW prioritization; clear Won't (v1) table with reasons; timeline and budget constraints cited.
scale.2: Prioritization clear, but Won't table has brief justifications.
scale.1: Prioritization lacks clear boundary between v1 and later scope.

criteria.name: Discovery Checklist Completeness
criteria.description: Coverage of Handbook 4.2.5 checklist: problem, personas, journeys, data ownership/retention, integrations, compliance, success definition in client's own words.

scale.3: Comprehensive coverage of all checklist areas including data retention, integrations, compliance, and client success quote.
scale.2: Most areas covered; 1 minor area (e.g. retention policy) not explicitly probed.
scale.1: Multiple major discovery areas missing (e.g. data ownership, success metrics).
scale.0: Superficial discovery covering only basic features.
